summary: Drag-to-order or click-to-rank. The respondent arranges items rather than choosing among them.
use_when: the request says rank, order, prioritise or drag
the output is a sequence rather than a selection
warnings: Interview only in this release. Scaffold from `basic`, then apply this archetype's questions and capture shape by hand; `basic` is the reference structure and every archetype inherits it.

questions.ask: Must every item be ranked, or may some be left out?
questions.why: A partial ranking needs an explicit unranked sentinel in the data, decided now rather than inferred later from blanks.
Drag needs touch support and a keyboard-accessible alternative; click-to-assign needs neither and is materially cheaper.

questions.ask: Is the rank recorded per item, or the item recorded per rank?
questions.why: They export differently and analysts assume one. Choosing wrong means re-processing every dataset.

questions.ask: Does a partially completed ranking need to survive a refresh?
questions.why: State kept only in memory is lost on refresh; persistence has to go through real capture variables.
